question: In a patient with DKA whose serum potassium is 3.2 mEq/L on admission, insulin infusion should be started immediately along with IV fluid replacement.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false — a critical safety rule. K+ <3.5 mEq/L in DKA = hold insulin. Start IV fluids and replenish potassium (20-40 mEq/h IV) until K+ ≥3.5 mEq/L, then start insulin infusion. Giving insulin with hypokalaemia can cause fatal cardiac arrhythmias.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Insulin drives potassium into cells, and starting insulin when K+ is already <3.5 mEq/L risks life-threatening hypokalaemia and cardiac arrhythmias. The rule: replace potassium to ≥3.5 mEq/L BEFORE starting insulin. Give IV fluids first, add potassium to the infusion, then commence insulin only when K+ ≥3.5.
